free_tier.stated: No number published. GitCode documents that it meters four resources per user — Git Repository Storage (all branches + all history, excluding LFS), Container Usage (core-hours), Git LFS Storage (all LFS-tracked files, all versions), and Project Count — with alerts at 80% and 95% of 'the quota'. The quota values themselves are only visible in the logged-in console.

egress.terms: Presumably free for public repos (standard for code hosts) but not stated. LFS reads go through the GitCode CDN.

tooling: git + git-lfs; a documented REST API (docs.gitcode.com/en/docs/repos); container registry. GitCode also mirrors ModelScope/HF repos, which is how most people touch it.
chaining: Per-user quota, so N accounts. But the practical ceiling is the per-file limit, not the account total: community docs put the web uploader at 10 MB per file and the default push limit at 100 MB, with LFS as the only path above that.
limits_note: 10 MB web upload, ~100 MB single-file push limit (community-documented, not in official docs), LFS for anything larger. Quota numbers unpublished and enforced with 80%/95% warnings. Usage resets monthly (statistics are calendar-month based).
reliability_note: Quota is enforced by silent rejection at the 95% mark with only an email warning; because the numbers are hidden until you hit them, this is a poor host for a planned multi-TB load.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: read live: the four metered resource types and 'When resource usage reaches 80% of the quota, the system will send a reminder ... When it reaches 95%, a warning notification'
third-party: '网页端上传文件时，单个文件最大不得超过 10MB ... GitCode 默认限制单文件大小上限 100MB'
